name: snap_kit
summary: Snapchat Snap Kit connector covering Login Kit (OAuth2 authorization-code flow against accounts.snapchat.com), Bitmoji Kit (2D/3D avatar CDN URL builder + api.bitmoji.com/avatar/json reference), and Creative Kit (snapchat://creativekit/share deeplink builder for sticker + caption + attachment passthrough). Stdlib-only (no `snapchat-py` dependency). Auth model: confidential OAuth2 client — Basic-auth client_id:client_secret on the token endpoint, bearer access_token on kit.snapchat.com/v1/me. The three local URL-builders (login_oauth2_url, bitmoji_avatar_url, creative_share_url) operate without network and without keys — they're pure string assembly so the dApp can preview consent + deeplink URLs even before user provisioning. verify_credentials() is also a no-network smoke that reports keys_present. Every successful network call (exchange_code / refresh_token / me) appends one InferenceRecord with tier='social_event', model='snap_kit', scope=f'snap_<tool>'. Graceful degrade: missing SNAP_CLIENT_ID + SNAP_CLIENT_SECRET → connect() returns False, network tools return SendResult(success=False, error='snap_kit_keys not configured') WITHOUT any urllib request; local builders still work (with a warning when client_id is absent).
engine_pattern: ThirdPartyConnector subclass mirroring stripe_mcp + deepseek_mcp shape exactly. SERVICE='snap_kit'. Form-encoded urllib POSTs to accounts.snapchat.com/accounts/oauth2/token (with Basic-auth header from base64(client_id:client_secret)) for the OAuth2 authorization_code + refresh_token grants. Bearer-auth GET to kit.snapchat.com/v1/me. Bitmoji CDN URL uses a deterministic template (images.bitmoji.com/3d/avatar/<ext_id>-v1.webp); api.bitmoji.com/avatar/json is referenced in metadata. Creative Kit share is a pure deeplink (snapchat://creativekit/share?...) — there's no server-side endpoint, the URL is consumed by a Snapchat client on the device. Tool dispatch via send(recipient=tool_name, message=json_args). Local-only tools are handled BEFORE the connect gate so they remain available without keys. connect() does NOT hit the network — Snap Kit's token endpoint rejects unauthenticated probes — successful connect just means both client_id and client_secret are loaded.

env_vars.SNAP_CLIENT_ID: Snap Kit OAuth2 client_id from Snap Kit Developer Portal → Your App → Configuration
env_vars.SNAP_CLIENT_SECRET: Snap Kit OAuth2 client_secret from the same panel; treat as bearer-equivalent

user_provisioning_required.rationale: SNAP_CLIENT_ID and SNAP_CLIENT_SECRET are user-issued credentials tied to a Snap Kit Developer account. They are NOT included in the shared .env today. Until Tom provisions them, connect() returns False and the network tools (exchange_code, refresh_token, me) graceful-fail every call without making any urllib request. The local URL-builders (login_oauth2_url, bitmoji_avatar_url, creative_share_url, verify_credentials) still work and emit the correct surfaces — login_oauth2_url just embeds a '<SNAP_CLIENT_ID>' placeholder with a warning.
how_to_obtain: 1. Visit https://kit.snapchat.com/portal and sign in with a Snapchat account.
2. Create or select an app, then go to Configuration → OAuth2 to find Client ID and Client Secret.
3. Add your redirect URI (e.g. https://trollz.fun/snap/callback) to the allowed Redirect URIs list — Snap Kit requires exact-match.
4. Request the scopes you need (default: user.display_name, user.bitmoji.avatar). For Bitmoji 3D add user.bitmoji.avatar; for external_id add user.external_id.
5. Production Snap Kit requires Snap review for live mode. Until then your app runs in staging mode and only allowlisted Snapchat accounts can authorize.

convenience_wrappers: verify_credentials()  — no-network smoke; returns {keys_present, has_client_id, has_client_secret, expected_tools, oauth_*_url, me_url}
login_oauth2_url(redirect_uri, state, scopes=['user.display_name','user.bitmoji.avatar'])  — local build of the Snapchat OAuth2 consent URL with state nonce
exchange_code(code, redirect_uri)  — POST /accounts/oauth2/token with Basic-auth + grant_type=authorization_code
me(access_token)  — GET kit.snapchat.com/v1/me with bearer; unwraps display_name + bitmoji.avatar + external_id
creative_share_url(sticker_id, caption, attachment_url)  — local snapchat://creativekit/share?... deeplink the caller hands off to a Snapchat client
substrate: studio/third_party/snap_kit/ (per-config persistence) + ~/.cc/third_party_logs/snap_kit_sends.jsonl (history) + ~/.cc/inference_master_chain.jsonl (crystal-anchored social_event records, tier='social_event', model='snap_kit')

outbound_calls: https://api.bitmoji.com/avatar/json                     (referenced for full avatar render — CDN template used locally)
snapchat://creativekit/share                            (deeplink scheme — built locally, opened by client)
routing_connections.substrate_reads: SNAP_CLIENT_ID + SNAP_CLIENT_SECRET via studio/auth/keys.load_env (and SNAPCHAT_CLIENT_ID/SECRET as os.environ fallback)
routing_connections.substrate_writes: send_log entries + crystal_chain social_event records (only when network tools succeed; local builders do not crystal-anchor)

guarantees: Crystal-anchored — every successful HTTP tool call has a deterministic InferenceRecord with tier='social_event', model='snap_kit', scope='snap_<tool>'
Stdlib-only — no `snapchat-py` or `requests` package required; uses urllib (form-encoded POST + JSON GET) + base64 for Basic auth

Graceful — missing SNAP_CLIENT_ID/SNAP_CLIENT_SECRET → connect() returns False and the three network tools return SendResult(success=False, error='snap_kit_keys not configured') WITHOUT any urllib request
Local builders always work — login_oauth2_url, bitmoji_avatar_url, creative_share_url, and verify_credentials are pure-stdlib URL assembly + state introspection; no network, no key requirement
Redacted logs — access_token, refresh_token, code, client_secret, id_token, authorization headers are stripped from the crystal-anchor payload via _redact()
State CSRF enforced — login_oauth2_url rejects requests missing the state nonce, surfacing the OAuth2 CSRF requirement at the connector boundary
Confidential client — token-endpoint POSTs use HTTP Basic auth (base64(client_id:client_secret)) per Snap Kit's OAuth2 confidential-client spec
usage_example:
from core.lib.third_party.snap_kit import SnapKitConnector
import json
c = SnapKitConnector()
r = c.send('verify_credentials', '')
print(r.success, r.metadata.get('keys_present'))
url_r = c.send('login_oauth2_url', json.dumps({'redirect_uri':'https://trollz.fun/snap/callback','state':'csrf-abc123','scopes':['user.display_name','user.bitmoji.avatar']}))
print(url_r.metadata['oauth2_url'])
if c.connect():
    tok = c.send('exchange_code', json.dumps({'code':'<from-callback>','redirect_uri':'https://trollz.fun/snap/callback'}))
    me  = c.send('me', json.dumps({'access_token':'<access-token-from-tok.body>'}))
    print(me.metadata.get('display_name'), me.metadata.get('bitmoji_avatar'))
    bm  = c.send('bitmoji_avatar_url', json.dumps({'external_id': me.metadata.get('external_id','')}))
    print(bm.metadata['avatar_url'])
    sh  = c.send('creative_share_url', json.dumps({'sticker_id':'sticker_42','caption':'gm','attachment_url':'https://trollz.fun/share/asset.png'}))
    print(sh.metadata['share_url'])
else:
    print('no SNAP_CLIENT_ID/SNAP_CLIENT_SECRET — set in .env to enable network tools')
